subproblems.title: Countably many C¹ charts inside U covering a set carried by embedded C¹ submanifolds (Lindelöf; parent Step 2)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M N₀ : Set (Euclid P)) (N : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → (∀ l, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m (N l)) → M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ l, N l → ∃ (V : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid P), (∀ s, IsOpen (V s) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (ψ s) (V s) ∧ InjOn (ψ s) (V s) ∧ (∀ y ∈ V s, Injective (fderiv ℝ (ψ s) y)) ∧ ψ s '' V s ⊆ U) ∧ M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ s, ψ s '' V s
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 2 (Simon Ch. 2, §4 (4.1) local representations; Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, chapter-03.txt lines 25–72).

A chart below is a pair (V', ψ') such that:
- V' ⊆ ℝ^m is open;
- ψ' is C¹ on V' and injective on V';
- Dψ'(y) is injective for every y ∈ V';
- ψ'(V') ⊆ U.

1. Local charts. Fix l ∈ ℕ and z ∈ N_l. The definition IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N_l, applied at z, gives:
   - an open V_{l,z} ⊆ ℝ^m;
   - an open W_{l,z} ⊆ ℝ^P with z ∈ W_{l,z};
   - a map ψ_{l,z} : ℝ^m → ℝ^P.
   They satisfy:
   - ψ_{l,z} is C¹ on V_{l,z}. The definition gives the order ((1 : ℕ) : WithTop ℕ∞), which equals 1 (Nat.cast_one; simpa).
   - ψ_{l,z} is injective on V_{l,z}.
   - ψ_{l,z}(V_{l,z}) = W_{l,z} ∩ N_l.
   - Dψ_{l,z}(y) is injective for every y ∈ V_{l,z}.
   The properness clause of the definition is not used. Choose such data for all (l, z) (axiom of choice).

2. Countable subcover. Fix l. The sets W_{l,z}, z ∈ N_l, are open in the second-countable space ℝ^P. Apply Lindelöf's property (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable) to the family z ↦ W_{l,z}, indexed by the subtype N_l. It gives a countable set T_l ⊆ N_l with ⋃_{z∈T_l} W_{l,z} = ⋃_{z∈N_l} W_{l,z}. Since z ∈ W_{l,z} for every z ∈ N_l, N_l ⊆ ⋃_{z∈T_l} W_{l,z}.

3. Shrinking into U. Let I := {(l, z) : l ∈ ℕ, z ∈ T_l}, formally the sigma type Σ l, T_l. It is countable, being a countable union of countable sets. For i = (l, z) ∈ I put V'_i := V_{l,z} ∩ ψ_{l,z}⁻¹(U) and ψ'_i := ψ_{l,z}.
   - V'_i is open: ψ_{l,z} is C¹, hence continuous, on the open set V_{l,z}, and U is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage).
   - Since V'_i ⊆ V_{l,z}:
     - ψ'_i is C¹ on V'_i (ContDiffOn.mono);
     - ψ'_i is injective on V'_i (InjOn.mono);
     - Dψ'_i(y) is injective for y ∈ V'_i.
   - ψ'_i(V'_i) ⊆ U by the definition of V'_i.
   So (V'_i, ψ'_i) is a chart.

4. Enumeration. Add one index ∗ with V'_∗ := ∅ and ψ'_∗ := 0. This is a chart, because every condition quantifies over the empty set: ∅ is open and ψ'_∗(∅) = ∅ ⊆ U. The index set I ∪ {∗} (formally Option I) is countable and nonempty, so there is a surjection σ : ℕ → I ∪ {∗} (exists_surjective_nat). Put V_s := V'_{σ(s)} and ψ_s := ψ'_{σ(s)}. By step 3 and the choice of ∗, every (V_s, ψ_s) satisfies the five chart properties of the conclusion.

5. Covering. Let x ∈ M. If x ∈ N₀ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise x ∈ N_l for some l, by the hypothesis M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_l N_l.
   - By step 2, x ∈ W_{l,z} for some z ∈ T_l. So x ∈ W_{l,z} ∩ N_l = ψ_{l,z}(V_{l,z}); write x = ψ_{l,z}(v) with v ∈ V_{l,z}.
   - Since x ∈ M ⊆ U, v ∈ ψ_{l,z}⁻¹(U), i.e. v ∈ V'_{(l,z)}.
   - Choose s with σ(s) = (l, z). Then v ∈ V_s and x = ψ_s(v) ∈ ψ_s(V_s).
   Hence M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_s ψ_s(V_s). ∎

proof_key_steps: From IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N_l choose a chart (V_{l,z}, W_{l,z}, ψ_{l,z}) at every z ∈ N_l, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N_l and order cast ↑1 = 1.
Lindelöf (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable): countably many W_{l,z}, z ∈ T_l, cover N_l.
Shrink the domain to V_{l,z} ∩ ψ_{l,z}⁻¹(U): it is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage), inherits the chart properties by mono, and has image ⊆ U.
Enumerate Option (Σ l, T_l) by a surjection from ℕ; the extra index carries the empty chart.
Each x ∈ M ∖ N₀ lies in some W_{l,z} ∩ N_l = ψ_{l,z}(V_{l,z}); its preimage lies in the shrunken domain because M ⊆ U.

subproblems.title: Compact pieces of a C¹ chart on which f∘ψ agrees with C¹ functions (C¹ approximation; parent Step 3)
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid m → ℝ) (K : NNReal), LipschitzWith K u → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ G : Euclid m → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 G ∧ volume {y | u y ≠ G y} < ε) → ∀ (m P : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → LipschitzWith L f → ∃ (C C' : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (F : ℕ → Euclid m → ℝ), (∀ k, IsCompact (C k) ∧ IsCompact (C' k) ∧ Convex ℝ (C' k) ∧ C k ⊆ interior (C' k) ∧ C' k ⊆ V ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 (F k) ∧ ∀ y ∈ C k, f (ψ y) = F k y) ∧ volume (V \ ⋃ k, C k) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 3. Simon Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2 'only if' (chapter-03.txt lines 36–50). Ch. 2, Theorem 1.2 (Lipschitz extension, chapter-02.txt line 33) and Theorem 1.5 (C¹ approximation, line 165); the latter is the antecedent (CA).

Notation: B̄_r(c) = closedBall c r and B_r(c) = ball c r.

1. Ball cover (Lindelöf). Let 𝔅 be the set of pairs b = (c_b, r_b) ∈ ℝ^m × ℝ with r_b > 0 and B̄_{2r_b}(c_b) ⊆ V.
   - Let v ∈ V. Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(v) ⊆ V (V is open). Then B̄_{2ε/3}(v) ⊆ B_ε(v) ⊆ V, so (v, ε/3) ∈ 𝔅 and v ∈ B_{ε/3}(v).
   - Hence V ⊆ ⋃_{b∈𝔅} B_{r_b}(c_b).
   - Lindelöf (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable, for the open balls B_{r_b}(c_b), b ∈ 𝔅) gives a countable T ⊆ 𝔅 with ⋃_{b∈T} B_{r_b}(c_b) = ⋃_{b∈𝔅} B_{r_b}(c_b) ⊇ V.

2. Lipschitz on a ball. Fix b ∈ T and write B̄ := B̄_{r_b}(c_b) and B̄' := B̄_{2r_b}(c_b).
   - B̄' is convex and compact, and B̄' ⊆ V, so ψ is C¹ on B̄' (ContDiffOn.mono).
   - A C¹ map on a convex compact set is Lipschitz there (ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith). So ψ is Λ_b-Lipschitz on B̄' for some Λ_b ≥ 0.
   - Hence u_b := f∘ψ is (LΛ_b)-Lipschitz on B̄', and therefore on B̄ ⊆ B̄' (since r_b ≤ 2r_b).

3. Lipschitz extension. By McShane's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.2; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) there is ũ_b : ℝ^m → ℝ, (LΛ_b)-Lipschitz on ℝ^m, with ũ_b = u_b on B̄. In particular ũ_b is continuous.

4. C¹ approximation. For each k ∈ ℕ apply (CA) to ũ_b (constant LΛ_b) with ε := (k+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞]. This gives a C¹ function G_{b,k} : ℝ^m → ℝ with L^m({ũ_b ≠ G_{b,k}}) < (k+1)⁻¹.

5. The pieces. For b ∈ T and k ∈ ℕ put
   - C_{b,k} := B̄ ∩ {y : ũ_b(y) = G_{b,k}(y)};
   - C'_{b,k} := B̄';
   - F_{b,k} := G_{b,k}.
   They have the following properties.
   - (i) The set {ũ_b = G_{b,k}} is closed, because both functions are continuous. So C_{b,k} is a closed subset of the compact set B̄, hence compact.
   - (ii) C'_{b,k} is compact and convex, and C'_{b,k} ⊆ V.
   - (iii) C_{b,k} ⊆ int B̄'. Every y ∈ B̄ satisfies |y − c_b| ≤ r_b < 2r_b, so y ∈ B_{2r_b}(c_b). That open ball lies in the interior of B̄' (ball_subset_interior_closedBall).
   - (iv) F_{b,k} is C¹.
   - (v) For y ∈ C_{b,k}: f(ψ(y)) = u_b(y) = ũ_b(y) = G_{b,k}(y), using y ∈ B̄.

6. Enumeration.
   - Add an index ∗ with C_∗ := C'_∗ := ∅ and F_∗ := 0. Properties (i)–(v) hold for ∗: ∅ is compact and convex, ∅ ⊆ int ∅ and ∅ ⊆ V, the zero function is C¹, and (v) is vacuous.
   - T × ℕ is countable, so (T × ℕ) ∪ {∗} (formally Option (T × ℕ)) is countable and nonempty. Let σ : ℕ → (T × ℕ) ∪ {∗} be surjective.
   - Put C_k := C_{σ(k)}, C'_k := C'_{σ(k)} and F_k := F_{σ(k)}. All per-k properties of the conclusion hold by step 5.

7. Null remainder.
   - Let v ∈ V ∖ ⋃_k C_k. By step 1, v ∈ B_{r_b}(c_b) ⊆ B̄_{r_b}(c_b) for some b ∈ T.
   - For every k ∈ ℕ choose s with σ(s) = (b, k). Since v ∉ C_s = C_{b,k} and v ∈ B̄_{r_b}(c_b), we get ũ_b(v) ≠ G_{b,k}(v).
   - Hence V ∖ ⋃_k C_k ⊆ ⋃_{b∈T} Z_b, where Z_b := ⋂_{k∈ℕ} {ũ_b ≠ G_{b,k}}.
   - For each b and every n ∈ ℕ, L^m(Z_b) ≤ L^m({ũ_b ≠ G_{b,n}}) < (n+1)⁻¹ ≤ n⁻¹.
   - If L^m(Z_b) ≠ 0, there is n with n⁻¹ < L^m(Z_b) (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt), a contradiction. So L^m(Z_b) = 0.
   - T is countable, and a countable union of null sets is null. So L^m(V ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. ∎

subproblems.title: C¹ maps on open sets send Lebesgue-null sets to H^m-null sets (Luzin N property)
subproblems.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^m open, ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P C¹ on V, and Z ⊆ V with L^m(Z) = 0, where L^m = volume on Euclid m. Then H^m(ψ(Z)) = 0, where H^m = μHE[m] is the normalized m-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (V Z : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → Z ⊆ V → volume Z = 0 → μHE[m] (ψ '' Z) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3 §2: 'if f is locally Lipschitz and B has Hⁿ-measure zero, then Hⁿ(f(B)) = 0' (chapter-03.txt, discussion after 2.4). Also Ch. 2, Theorem 1.8(i), the Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).

1. Local Lipschitz neighbourhoods. Let y ∈ V. Since V is open, V is a neighbourhood of y, so ψ is C¹ at y (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). Hence ψ is Lipschitz on some neighbourhood of y (ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith). Shrinking it to an open subset, there are an open t_y ∋ y and K_y ≥ 0 such that ψ is K_y-Lipschitz on t_y.

2. Countable subcover. Apply Lindelöf (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable) to the open family (t_y)_{y∈V}. It gives a countable T ⊆ V with ⋃_{y∈T} t_y = ⋃_{y∈V} t_y ⊇ V ⊇ Z.

3. Hence ψ(Z) ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T} ψ(Z ∩ t_y), a countable union.

4. Fix y ∈ T. ψ is K_y-Lipschitz on Z ∩ t_y ⊆ t_y. By the Lipschitz image bound for the normalized Hausdorff measure, H^m(ψ(Z ∩ t_y)) ≤ K_y^m · H^m(Z ∩ t_y). On the domain ℝ^m = Euclid m, μHE[m] equals Lebesgue measure L^m (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Since Z ∩ t_y ⊆ Z and L^m(Z) = 0, the right-hand side is 0.

5. By countable subadditivity (measure_biUnion_null_iff, T countable), H^m(ψ(Z)) ≤ Σ_{y∈T} H^m(ψ(Z ∩ t_y)) = 0. ∎

Remark: Mathlib's DifferentiableOn.hausdorffMeasure_image_eq_zero would also give the result, together with μHE[m] = c·μH[m] for some c ≠ 0. It needs `import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffDimension`, which is not in the contract's import closure, so the self-contained route above is used.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of M on a chart piece via (TL) (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2); parent Step 7)

Source: parent proof Step 7. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 86–140), with (TL) in place of the upper-density argument.

1. The set S. S := ψ(C') is compact, because ψ is C¹, hence continuous, on the compact set C'. So S is closed and Borel. S ⊆ U by hypothesis.

2. S has finite measure.
   - ψ is C¹ on the convex compact set C', so it is Λ-Lipschitz on C' for some Λ ≥ 0 (ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith).
   - By the Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), H^m(S) ≤ Λ^m · H^m(C').
   - On Euclid m, H^m(C') = L^m(C') (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and L^m(C') < ∞ because C' is compact.
   - So H^m(S ∩ K) ≤ H^m(S) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.

3. The set A := M ∩ ψ(C).
   - ψ(C) is compact (C is compact, C ⊆ C', ψ is continuous on C'), so A is Borel.
   - A ⊆ ψ(C) ⊆ ψ(C') = S, because C ⊆ int C' ⊆ C'.
   - A ⊆ M.

4. First application of (TL), with (P, n, U, A, B) := (P, m, U, A, S). Its hypotheses hold: U is open, A and S are Borel, A ⊆ S ⊆ U, and H^m(S ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (step 2). Hence, for μHE[m]⌞A-a.e. x and every subspace Q: S has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A has approximate tangent space Q at x.

5. Second application of (TL), with (P, m, U, A, M). Its hypotheses hold: M is Borel, A ⊆ M ⊆ U, and H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U by hypothesis. Hence, for μHE[m]⌞A-a.e. x and every Q: M has Q at x iff A has Q at x.

6. Conclusion.
   - The intersection of the two full-measure sets of steps 4 and 5 again has full μHE[m]⌞A-measure (filter_upwards).
   - Let x be in it and y ∈ C with ψ(y) = x. Since y ∈ C ⊆ int C', (IT) says that S = ψ(C') has approximate tangent space Q := Dψ(y)(ℝ^m) at ψ(y) = x.
   - By step 4, A has Q at x; by step 5, M has Q at x. ∎

subproblems.title: Derivative bound |DF(y)e| ≤ L|Dψ(y)e| at a.e. point of a set where F = f∘ψ (parent Step 8)
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (d : ℕ) (Z : Set (Euclid d)) (y : Euclid d), Tendsto (fun r => volume (Z ∩ closedBall y r) / volume (closedBall y r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → ∀ v : Euclid d, ‖v‖ = 1 → ∃ ys : ℕ → Euclid d, (∀ i, ys i ∈ Z ∧ ys i ≠ y) ∧ Tendsto ys atTop (𝓝 y) ∧ Tendsto (fun i => ‖ys i - y‖⁻¹ • (ys i - y)) atTop (𝓝 v)) → ∀ (m P : ℕ) (Z : Set (Euclid m)) (F : Euclid m → ℝ) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), MeasurableSet Z → (∀ y ∈ Z, DifferentiableAt ℝ F y ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ y) → (∀ y ∈ Z, f (ψ y) = F y) → LipschitzWith L f → ∀ᵐ y ∂volume, y ∈ Z → ∀ e : Euclid m, |fderiv ℝ F y e| ≤ (L : ℝ) * ‖fderiv ℝ ψ y e‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 8 (= Step 3(a) of the slice-family proof); Lebesgue density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet).

1. Density points.
   - Lebesgue measure L^m on ℝ^m is locally finite, and ℝ^m has the Besicovitch covering property. Since Z is Borel, Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet gives: for L^m-a.e. y, L^m(Z ∩ B̄_r(y))/L^m(B̄_r(y)) → 1_Z(y) as r ↓ 0 (filter 𝓝[>] 0).
   - Fix such a y with y ∈ Z. Then the limit is 1, i.e. y satisfies the density hypothesis of (DD).
   - It suffices to prove the bound at this y.

2. Unit directions. Let v ∈ ℝ^m with |v| = 1. By (DD), with (d, Z', y', v) := (m, Z, y, v), there are y_i ∈ Z with y_i ≠ y and y_i → y, such that w_i := t_i⁻¹(y_i − y) → v, where t_i := |y_i − y| > 0.

3. Lipschitz comparison. For each i, y and y_i lie in Z, so |F(y_i) − F(y)| = |f(ψ(y_i)) − f(ψ(y))| ≤ L·|ψ(y_i) − ψ(y)|. Multiplying by t_i⁻¹ ≥ 0 gives |t_i⁻¹(F(y_i) − F(y))| ≤ L·|t_i⁻¹(ψ(y_i) − ψ(y))|.

4. Difference quotients.
   - Put d_i := y_i − y and c_i := t_i⁻¹. Then d_i → 0, c_i·d_i = w_i → v, and y + d_i = y_i.
   - F has derivative DF(y) at y, so c_i(F(y + d_i) − F(y)) → DF(y)v (HasFDerivWithinAt.lim with s = ℝ^m, from the HasFDerivAt given by differentiability).
   - Likewise c_i(ψ(y + d_i) − ψ(y)) → Dψ(y)v.
   - Direct argument: F(y + d_i) − F(y) − DF(y)d_i = o(|d_i|) and |c_i d_i| = 1, so c_i(F(y + d_i) − F(y)) − DF(y)w_i → 0. Also DF(y)w_i → DF(y)v by continuity of DF(y).

5. Limit. Absolute value and norm are continuous, and non-strict inequalities pass to the limit (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'). So step 3 yields |DF(y)v| ≤ L·|Dψ(y)v|.

6. General e. If e = 0, both sides vanish. Otherwise v := |e|⁻¹e has |v| = 1. By linearity of DF(y) and Dψ(y), |e|⁻¹|DF(y)e| = |DF(y)v| ≤ L|Dψ(y)v| = |e|⁻¹·L|Dψ(y)e|. Multiply by |e| > 0. ∎

subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (C : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid P) (Good : ℕ → Euclid m → Prop), MeasurableSet M → (∀ j, IsCompact (C j) ∧ ContinuousOn (ψ j) (C j)) → μ (M \ ⋃ j, ψ j '' C j) = 0 → (∀ j, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict (M ∩ ψ j '' C j)), ∀ y ∈ C j, ψ j y = x → Good j y) → ∃ Y : ℕ → Set (Euclid m), (∀ j, MeasurableSet (Y j) ∧ Y j ⊆ C j ∧ ψ j '' Y j ⊆ M ∧ ∀ y ∈ Y j, Good j y) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (ψ i '' Y i) (ψ j '' Y j)) ∧ μ (M \ ⋃ j, ψ j '' Y j) = 0

Source: parent proof Steps 4–6; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 67–72).

1. Images. E_j := ψ_j(C_j) is compact, as the continuous image of a compact set. So E_j is closed and Borel, and A_j := M ∩ E_j is Borel.

2. Exceptional sets.
   - Let p_j(x) mean: every y ∈ C_j with ψ_j(y) = x satisfies Good_j(y). The hypothesis says μ⌞A_j({x : ¬p_j(x)}) = 0.
   - By exists_measurable_superset_of_null, applied to the measure μ⌞A_j, choose a Borel set T_j ⊇ {x : ¬p_j(x)} with μ⌞A_j(T_j) = 0.
   - Since T_j is Borel, μ⌞A_j(T_j) = μ(T_j ∩ A_j) (Measure.restrict_apply). So μ(T_j ∩ A_j) = 0.

3. Disjointification (Remark 1.3). Let D_j := A_j ∖ ⋃_{i<j} A_i (Mathlib disjointed A j). Then:
   - the D_j are Borel (MeasurableSet.disjointed);
   - they are pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed);
   - D_j ⊆ A_j (disjointed_subset);
   - ⋃_j D_j = ⋃_j A_j (iUnion_disjointed).

7. Properties.
   - Y_j ⊆ C_j by definition.
   - ψ_j(Y_j) = M'_j ⊆ D_j ⊆ A_j ⊆ M.
   - Good points: let y ∈ Y_j and x := ψ_j(y) ∈ M'_j. Then x ∉ T_j ⊇ {¬p_j}, so p_j(x) holds. Applying p_j(x) to y (y ∈ C_j and ψ_j(y) = x) gives Good_j(y).
   - Disjointness: for i ≠ j, ψ_i(Y_i) = M'_i ⊆ D_i and ψ_j(Y_j) ⊆ D_j, which are disjoint.

8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ ⋃_j ψ_j(Y_j).
   - If x ∉ ⋃_j E_j, then x ∈ M ∖ ⋃_j E_j.
   - Otherwise x ∈ M ∩ E_{j₀} = A_{j₀} for some j₀. So x ∈ ⋃_j A_j = ⋃_j D_j, and x ∈ D_j for some j. Since x ∉ ψ_j(Y_j) = M'_j = D_j ∖ T_j, we get x ∈ T_j, and x ∈ D_j ⊆ A_j.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 9: Φ_j(y) = Dψ_j(y)Γ_j(y)⁻¹∇F_j(y) with Γ_j = Dψ_jᵀDψ_j, the defining identity, and |g| ≤ L. Simon Ch. 2, §4 (gradient ∇^N on a submanifold) and Ch. 3, 2.1.

Notation. E := ℝ^m and H := ℝ^P are finite-dimensional, hence complete, real inner product spaces. For y ∈ ℝ^m:
- A(y) := Dψ(y) : E → H;
- A(y)* : H → E is its adjoint (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint), so ⟨A(y)*h, e⟩ = ⟨h, A(y)e⟩;
- Γ(y) := A(y)* ∘ A(y) : E → E;
- a(y) := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm (DF(y)) is the Riesz vector of DF(y), so ⟨a(y), e⟩ = DF(y)e;
- Γ(y)⁻¹ := Ring.inverse Γ(y) in the Banach algebra E →L[ℝ] E (the inverse if Γ(y) is a unit, 0 otherwise).

1. Definition. Φ(y) := A(y)(Γ(y)⁻¹a(y)) for every y ∈ ℝ^m.

2. Γ(y) is a unit for y ∈ V.
   - If Γ(y)e = 0, then 0 = ⟨Γ(y)e, e⟩ = ⟨A(y)e, A(y)e⟩ = |A(y)e|². So A(y)e = 0, and e = 0 because Dψ(y) is injective.
   - Thus the endomorphism Γ(y) of the finite-dimensional space E has trivial kernel, so it is invertible as a linear map (LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot). Hence it is a unit of E →L[ℝ] E (ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_toLinearMap).
   - Writing Γ(y) = u for a unit u, Ring.inverse Γ(y) = u⁻¹ (Ring.inverse_unit), and Γ(y)(Γ(y)⁻¹v) = v for every v.

3. Defining identity. Fix y ∈ V and put w := Γ(y)⁻¹a(y), so Γ(y)w = a(y) by step 2.
   - Φ(y) = A(y)w ∈ range A(y) = Dψ(y)(ℝ^m).
   - For e ∈ E: ⟨Φ(y), A(y)e⟩ = ⟨A(y)w, A(y)e⟩ = ⟨A(y)*A(y)w, e⟩ = ⟨Γ(y)w, e⟩ = ⟨a(y), e⟩ = DF(y)e (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left).

4. Norm bound. Let L ≥ 0 with |DF(y)e| ≤ L·|A(y)e| for all e. With w as in step 3: |Φ(y)|² = ⟨Φ(y), A(y)w⟩ = DF(y)w ≤ |DF(y)w| ≤ L·|A(y)w| = L·|Φ(y)|. If |Φ(y)| = 0, then |Φ(y)| ≤ L because L ≥ 0. Otherwise divide by |Φ(y)| > 0.

5. Continuity on V.
   - (i) y ↦ A(y) is continuous on V, because ψ is C¹ on the open set V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
   - (ii) The adjoint operation is a linear isometric equivalence (E →L H) ≃ (H →L E), hence continuous. So y ↦ A(y)* is continuous on V.
   - (iii) Composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, so y ↦ Γ(y) is continuous on V (ContinuousOn.clm_comp).
   - (iv) In the complete normed ring E →L[ℝ] E, Ring.inverse is continuous at every unit (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). Since Γ(y) is a unit for y ∈ V (step 2), y ↦ Γ(y)⁻¹ is continuous on V.
   - (v) y ↦ DF(y) is continuous on ℝ^m because F is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), and toDual.symm is continuous. So y ↦ a(y) is continuous.
   - (vi) Evaluation (T, v) ↦ Tv is jointly continuous (ContinuousOn.clm_apply). So y ↦ Γ(y)⁻¹a(y) is continuous on V, and then so is y ↦ A(y)(Γ(y)⁻¹a(y)) = Φ(y). ∎

subproblems.title: Borel gluing of chart fields over disjoint injective images (Lusin–Souslin; parent Step 9)
subproblems.statement:
Let m, P ∈ ℕ, and for each j ∈ ℕ let Y_j ⊆ ℝ^m be Borel and ψ_j, Φ_j : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, with ψ_j continuous and injective on Y_j and Φ_j continuous on Y_j. Assume the sets ψ_j(Y_j) are pairwise disjoint.

Then there is a Borel measurable g : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that:
- g(ψ_j(y)) = Φ_j(y) for every j and every y ∈ Y_j;
- g(x) = 0 for every x ∉ ⋃_j ψ_j(Y_j).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (Y : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (ψ Φ : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid P), (∀ j, MeasurableSet (Y j) ∧ ContinuousOn (ψ j) (Y j) ∧ InjOn (ψ j) (Y j) ∧ ContinuousOn (Φ j) (Y j)) → Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (ψ i '' Y i) (ψ j '' Y j)) → ∃ g : Euclid P → Euclid P, Measurable g ∧ (∀ j, ∀ y ∈ Y j, g (ψ j y) = Φ j y) ∧ ∀ x, (∀ j, x ∉ ψ j '' Y j) → g x = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 9 ('g is Borel'). Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn, ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding). Countable piecewise gluing (Mathlib Measurable.find). Write M_j := ψ_j(Y_j).

1. Measurable embeddings.
   - ℝ^m is a Polish space. For each j, ψ_j is continuous and injective on the Borel set Y_j.
   - By the Lusin–Souslin theorem, the restriction e_j := ψ_j|_{Y_j} : Y_j → ℝ^P maps Borel subsets of Y_j to Borel subsets of ℝ^P. It is also measurable, so it is a measurable embedding (ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding).
   - In particular M_j is Borel (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).

2. One piece.
   - Φ_j|_{Y_j} : Y_j → ℝ^P is continuous (continuousOn_iff_continuous_restrict), hence Borel.
   - Let g_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the extension of Φ_j|_{Y_j} along e_j by the zero function (Function.extend). So g_j(e_j(y)) = Φ_j(y) for y ∈ Y_j, which is well defined because e_j is injective, and g_j(x) = 0 for x ∉ M_j.
   - The extension of a measurable function along a measurable embedding by a measurable function is measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend). So g_j is Borel.
   - g_j(ψ_j(y)) = Φ_j(y) for every y ∈ Y_j (Injective.extend_apply).

3. Gluing. Index the pieces by n ∈ ℕ:
   - piece 0 is the Borel set R := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_j M_j, with component function f_0 := 0;
   - piece j+1 is M_j, with component function f_{j+1} := g_j.
   Every x ∈ ℝ^P lies in some piece. Let n(x) be the least n such that x lies in piece n, and put g(x) := f_{n(x)}(x).
   - All pieces and all component functions are Borel. By Mathlib's Measurable.find, a function glued this way from countably many pieces is Borel.
   - Explicitly, for Borel B, g⁻¹(B) = ⋃_n ({x : n(x) = n} ∩ f_n⁻¹(B)), and {x : n(x) = n} = piece n ∖ ⋃_{k<n} piece k is Borel.

4. Values on M_j. Let y ∈ Y_j and x := ψ_j(y) ∈ M_j.
   - x ∉ R.
   - x ∉ M_i for i ≠ j, by pairwise disjointness.
   So piece j+1 is the only piece containing x, n(x) = j+1, and g(x) = g_j(x) = Φ_j(y) by step 2.

5. Zero elsewhere. If x ∉ ⋃_j M_j, then x ∈ R = piece 0, so n(x) = 0 and g(x) = 0. ∎
